features.feature: Sequential stages and direct executable steps
Persistent build history and stage/step state
Retry completed builds with preserved parameters
features.notes: A retry creates a new build and reuses persisted non-secret parameters; secret parameters require explicit replacement values, while richer retry policies and attempt grouping remain planned.

features.feature: Timestamped bounded stdout and stderr streaming
features.notes: Direct child output is streamed separately and one unterminated line is capped at 64 KiB with an explicit truncation marker, preventing unbounded memory growth.

features.feature: Priority queue with FIFO ties and global/per-project limits
features.notes: Higher bounded priorities run before older lower-priority work while equal priorities retain FIFO order; queued cancellation and authenticated pause/resume administration are handled before execution. Remote executor, CPU, and memory requirements are validated, matched against explicit agent capacity, and reserved atomically. Stage dependencies are validated for unknown references, duplicates, self-dependencies, and cycles, then executed in stable topological order; independent stages now run concurrently with cancellation and failure propagation. Richer local resource dimensions remain planned.

features.feature: Build artifact collection, checksums, and download
features.notes: Local workspace artifacts are copied into build-scoped storage and exposed through the API. Remote agents package declared matches into bounded checksum-verified chunks before the server validates and stores them; explicit age-ordered pruning of completed-build artifacts is available, while remote object stores remain planned.
Validated locally on Unix; remote agents and container execution are planned.

Exact relative cache paths and bounded primary/fallback keys are validated, entries are isolated by project and key, restoration tries the first valid archive before execution, saves are atomic after success, and an explicit local prune command removes only oldest regular archives under a byte budget; remote backends remain planned.

Container declarations validate an image, select Docker or Podman, and assemble a direct runtime run command with a bounded workspace mount, separated arguments, timeout propagation, and automatic removal; daemon execution, image policy, and end-to-end artifact/cancellation behavior remain unverified locally.

A versioned, non-executing analyzer reports line-level supported, partial, and unsupported findings, exposes them through the headless API and desktop report, and can generate a valid draft for simple quoted sh/bat steps, static environment assignments, string/password parameters, and safe archive patterns; dynamic values, typed parameter behavior, full Groovy/plugin interpretation, and broad generated Rivetfile conversion remain planned.

Explicit local clone, fetch, detached revision checkout, clean preparation, recursive submodule initialization, and bounded provider refspec fetches are supported through the SCM boundary and CLI/build admission paths. A provider-neutral credential ID can resolve through Rivet's encrypted local vault and reach Git through ephemeral HTTP Basic configuration; signed GitHub and GitLab push plus PR/MR adapters can feed the same build admission path with an explicit project route. Credential lifecycle and broader provider event mapping remain planned.

features.feature: Manual/API builds and persistent UTC cron schedules
features.notes: Five-field cron expressions are validated, persisted, atomically claimed, and exposed through API, CLI, and desktop controls. Schedules can either admit a build every occurrence or run the authenticated repository poller with persisted remote, fetch, and opaque credential-ID options; polling admits only an unrecorded exact Git revision. Signed provider PR/MR actions are normalized into real builds, while broader repository-event and upstream trigger mapping remain planned.

The generic endpoint verifies HMAC-SHA256 over the raw request body, atomically deduplicates event IDs, and queues one real build; provider adapters are tracked separately and broader repository-event mapping remains planned.

features.feature: Signed GitHub and GitLab push, pull-request, and merge-request adapters
features.notes: Explicit project routes normalize GitHub push/pull_request deliveries and GitLab Push Hook/Tag Push Hook/Merge Request Hook deliveries into the common idempotent build path. GitHub HMAC-SHA256 and GitLab signed webhook headers are verified over the raw body, provider head refs are fetched through bounded refspecs, optional fetch credential IDs are attached, and stale/invalid messages are rejected; broader provider event coverage remains planned.

A project-scoped authenticated endpoint inspects the local Git checkout, optionally fetches an explicit remote with a vault credential ID, compares the observed revision with the latest build, queues the exact revision, and durably deduplicates concurrent or repeated transitions. Persistent repository-poll schedules reuse those bounded options at dispatch time; provider-side event delivery and upstream lifecycle mapping remain planned.

features.feature: Versioned agent registration, assignment, and remote execution
features.notes: Agents negotiate a versioned protocol, advertise capabilities including optional CPU and memory capacity, reconnect with bounded backoff and session fencing, appear online or stale, and match only when capability and available resource requirements pass through POST /api/v1/agents/match. Remote builds reserve matching executor/CPU/memory capacity, transfer bounded workspaces and declared artifact bundles, execute through the shared Rust runner, relay typed events and output, and propagate cancellation. The session transport uses delivery IDs, ACKs, bounded duplicate suppression, and timed retransmission; a disconnect gets at most one replacement-agent attempt, while durable cross-session recovery remains planned.

Public liveness and SQLite-backed readiness probes, optional in-memory Bearer-token protection, mandatory authentication for non-loopback binds, exact CORS origins, request limits, baseline security headers, and private policy files with digest-backed tokens, project-scoped route authorization, Argon2id local user accounts, password login, persisted opaque sessions, and bounded admin-only authentication audit history are supported; external identity providers remain planned.

features.feature: Secret parameter redaction and log masking
features.notes: Secret parameters require runtime input without defaults, are redacted in persisted build/API data, masked in emitted process output, and must be supplied again for retries. SCM credentials can be stored as authenticated ciphertext in a passphrase-encrypted local vault, referenced by ID, and rotated or removed through an administrator-only API with bounded audit events; project allow-lists and an OS-keychain-backed vault passphrase source with validated deployment-specific service/account selection are supported, while target-OS keychain prompts/ACLs and richer ownership workflows remain planned.

The CLI reads a passphrase and secret from private regular files, stores only authenticated ciphertext, lists metadata without secrets, and the server resolves non-secret IDs for Git fetches. The server also exposes administrator-only list/replace/remove operations with audit events that never record the secret. Project allow-lists and an OS-keychain-backed vault passphrase source are supported, with explicit service/account selection and validation for deployment isolation; target-OS keychain prompts/ACLs and richer ownership workflows remain planned.
Rivet will define a versioned extension protocol instead of reproducing the Java plugin ABI.

Manifests, explicit permissions, bounded length-prefixed JSON frames, a direct-argument subprocess host, bounded local catalog discovery/API, a desktop model, a root-confined subprocess lifecycle manager with per-request permission enforcement, server/desktop lifecycle controls, a capability-free WASM ABI with bounded memory/output and fuel metering, bounded read-only builds/details/logs/artifacts host methods, persisted stage-scoped annotation host writes, and permission-checked real build triggering are present. This remains a Rivet extension boundary, not the Jenkins Java plugin ABI.

The harness validates bounded JSON snapshots, normalizes provider status spelling, line endings, checksum prefixes, and redaction markers, then returns a non-zero result for semantic differences. CLI adapters capture Rivet and Jenkins HTTP build/stage/artifact metadata with private token-file authentication and bounded responses; a local smoke test exercises a real Rivet server plus a protocol-compatible Jenkins fixture. A permanent corpus from deployed Jenkins remains planned.
